Welcome to a Meeting of the California Fish and Game Commission!
This year marks the 157th year of operation of the California Fish and Game Commission
(Commission) in partnership with the California Department of Fish and Wildlife. The
Commission’s goal is preserving our heritage and conserving our natural resources through
informed decision making; Commission meetings are vital in achieving that goal. In that spirit,
we provide the following information to be as effective and efficient as possible.

We expect to hear comments from people with varied perspectives and deeply held values
about California’s wildlife, coastal places, and public trust resources. In these meetings, the
Commission is committed to supporting an environment where everyone can safely participate,
while also protecting free speech. Meeting goals, expectations, and participation information
have been created to support a respectful, constructive environment where all voices are
heard; we share them here to enhance transparency.

Meeting Goals
•   Provide a safe and inclusive environment for sharing knowledge, experiences, ideas, and
    perspectives.
•   Uphold the Commission’s Justice, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion (JEDI) Policy and goals,
    including centering principles of environmental justice and access for underserved
    communities; recognizing and honoring the perspectives and traditional knowledge and
    practices of California tribes and tribal communities; and working from a shared
    understanding of key JEDI-related definitions and terms.
•   Ensure all commissioners can hear and participate in agenda topic dialogue in real time.


                                                 2

•   Daylight areas of agreement or disagreement, as well as potential modifications and
    compromises.
•   Gather input to inform Commission decision-making.

MPA Petitions Goals and Guidelines
•   Deliberate and vote on all actions within the 15 bin 2 MPA petitions. Decisions could be to
    grant and continue to a regulatory process, deny, or take any other action the Commission
    determines is warranted by the petition such as considering regulatory amendments that
    petitioners have suggested during the petition process, or granting or further reviewing
    some portions of a petition.
•   Consider MPA petitions on:
    - Wednesday in the afternoon (petition numbers 2023-14, 2023-23, 2023-33);
    - Thursday (petition numbers 2023-21, 2023-19, 2023-20, 2023-34, 2023-28, 2023-29,
      2022-04, and 2023-18 [Vandenberg and Kashtayit]); and
    - Friday (petition numbers 2023-27, 2023-18 [San Miguel and Anacapa special closures],
      2023-15, 2023-16, 2023-32, and 2023-24).
•   MPA petition agenda items will include an introduction to the subject, public comment, and
    Commission discussion and action.
•   Ceding time will be allowed for the MPA petition agenda items (beginning with Agenda
    Item 26).
    - If five or more people cede their time to a spokesperson, the speaker will receive 3
      minutes of speaking time and if four people cede their time to a spokesperson, the
      speaker will receive 2 minutes of speaking time.
    - For those attending in person, the speaker and those ceding time must submit their
      speaker cards all together at the staff table in front of the auditorium, before the agenda
      item is announced, even if you have pre-registered.
    - For those attending via Zoom, the speaker and those ceding time must either pre-
      register or send an email message to fgc@fgc.ca.gov no later than noon on Monday,
      October 12; in both cases, include your name, the spokesperson’s name, and the
      agenda item number.
•   At any time, the presiding commissioner may ask for visual cues (such as raising hands or
    standing up) to express support or opposition.
•   Pre-registration will be available on the Commission meeting webpage beginning
    Wednesday, September 30 until noon on Monday, October 12.
•   It is highly advised to submit written comments by September 30; if you also speak at the
    meeting, then you can simply highlight the key points of your written comments when giving
    oral comments.

Meeting Expectations: Commitment to a Respectful Environment and Free
Speech
We acknowledge that meeting participants care deeply about California’s wildlife, coastal
places, and public trust resources. The Commission is committed to creating and maintaining


                                                3

an environment where all participants feel safe, respected, and able to contribute meaningfully.
Therefore, the Commission strongly discourages personal attacks, intimidation, harassment,
hateful expressions (including racial or other identity-based comments), or other conduct or
comments that target individuals rather than issues. These comments can diminish the quality
of public dialogue, discourage community participation, and potentially reduce the likelihood
that commissioners will give weight to comments delivered in this manner.

The Commission upholds the right to free speech; all individuals possess this right and are
entitled to use their full speaking time to express their views, including critiques, alternative
perspectives, and disagreement. However, disruptions to the meeting will not be tolerated.
Personal threats or attacks on members, staff or other commenters, references to protected
characteristics, offensive or profane speech, yelling, interruptions, audible reactions, or
disputing another speaker during their speaking time may constitute a disruption to the
meeting, depending on the circumstances.

The Commission may restrict an individual’s right to speak when necessary to avoid disrupting
the orderly conduct of the meeting. In these cases, the presiding commissioner may gavel or
mute a speaker’s microphone. If the disruptive behavior continues, after a call for decorum and
a warning, the person or people disrupting the orderly conduct of the meeting may be removed
from the meeting, the meeting may be suspended, and the room may be cleared.

Meeting Participation: How to Engage and Attend
How to Provide Written Comments and Submission Deadlines

The public is encouraged to submit written comments on any agenda item. Written comments
can be more detailed than what time allows during verbal comment at the meeting, creating an
opportunity to share more information in support of your thoughts and ideas.

You may submit written comments by one of three methods (only one is necessary):
   1.       Email to fgc@fgc.ca.gov;
   2.       mail to California Fish and Game Commission, P.O. Box 944209, Sacramento, CA
            94244-2090; or
   3.       hand deliver to California Fish and Game Commission, 715 P Street, 16th floor,
            Sacramento, CA 95814 (call at least one business day in advance to arrange delivery).

Written Comment Deadlines

                   Comment Deadline*                  Supplemental Comment Deadline**

                  September 30, 5:00 PM                      October 8, 12:00 PM

        *    Written comments received at the Commission office by the Comment Deadline
             will be made available to the Commissioners prior to the meeting, and may be
             posted online with meeting materials.
        ** Written comments received at the Commission office by the Supplemental
             Comment Deadline will be made available to Commissioners at the meeting but
             not posted with meeting materials.



                                                  4

After the Supplemental Comment Deadline, written comments may be delivered in person to
the meeting. Please bring twelve (12) copies of written comments and hand them to the
designated staff member just prior to speaking.

Materials provided to the Commission will be available to the general public.

Visual Presentations: Slides, Videos, and Graphics

No visual presentations will be approved for the MPA petition agenda items (beginning with
Agenda Item 26); however, print copies of informational materials can be distributed to
commissioners and staff just before you speak by providing 12 copies to the identified staff
member.

All electronic presentations for non-MPA petition agenda items must be requested and
submitted by the Supplemental Comment Deadline and approved by the Commission
executive director before the meeting.

•   Electronic presentations must be provided by email to fgc@fgc.ca.gov. If the file is too large
    to send via email, contact staff to identify an alternative method for submitting the file.
•   Specify to which meeting date and agenda topic it pertains.
•   All electronic formats must be Windows PC compatible.
•   If presenting in person, it is recommended that you bring a print copy of your presentation
    in case of technical difficulties.
•   Pursuant to the Commission’s meeting procedures, approval is at the discretion of the
    president and is not guaranteed.

Participate in Person, on Zoom, or by Phone
All Commission meetings are open to the public and subject to the Bagley-Keene Open
Meeting Act. You may participate and comment in person, via Zoom webinar, or by phone;
meetings are also live streamed for listening or viewing only. The presiding commissioner will
explain how to indicate your interest in speaking and time limits. Staff expects to be available
to assist with logistical questions in person at the external staff table, by phone at (916) 653-
4899, or by email at fgc@fgc.ca.gov. After each meeting, audio and video archives are posted
to the Commission website.

How to Provide Verbal Comment During the Meeting
•   Pre-Register: This is the best way to ensure you are on the list of speakers, whether you
    are joining in person, via Zoom, or on the phone! No need to fill out a speaker card for each
    agenda item and no worrying about whether you have missed the queue to raise your hand
    in Zoom. Pre-registration begins Wednesday, September 30 and ends at noon on Monday,
    October 12.

•   In Person: Complete a “speaker card” — available outside the meeting room near the
    entrance — and submit it at the staff table at the bottom of the ramp just outside the
    auditorium. If others are ceding time to you, they must be present when you submit your
    speaker card. Please complete one speaker card per agenda item. You must submit your
    speaker card before the agenda item is announced. In-person speakers will be called in



                                                5

small groups. Please line up behind the podium when your name is called and note that the
    order of speakers does not matter.

•   Via Zoom or Phone: A “call for public comment” will be made at the beginning of each
    agenda item, specifying an approximately three-minute time window to “raise” your hand.
    Please raise your hand either through the Zoom function or, if on the phone, by pressing *9
    once on your phone when prompted at the beginning of the agenda item. You must be
    available online at the beginning of the agenda item to raise your hand during the
    allotted time window.

•   General Public Comment for Items Not on the Agenda: Comments made during the general
    public comment agenda items (Tuesday morning and Friday afternoon) must be about
    matters not on this agenda. This time is an opportunity to bring other issues to the
    Commission’s attention; concerns may also be submitted by email or mail. Note that the
    Commission may not discuss or take action on any matter raised during this item, except to
    decide whether to place the matter on the agenda of a future meeting (per sections 11125
    and 11125.7(a), California Government Code).

Accessibility or Accommodation Needs
Individuals with disabilities and/or needing reasonable accommodation to participate in
Commission meetings may contact the Civil Rights Office (CRO) of the California Department
of Fish and Wildlife at civilrights@wildlife.ca.gov. Requests for facility or meeting accessibility
and requests for American Sign Language interpreters should be submitted at least two weeks
before the meeting to help ensure that the requested accommodation can be met. Requests
for real-time captioners should be submitted at least four weeks prior to the event. These
timeframes are to help ensure that the requested accommodation can be met. If an
accommodation is no longer needed, please notify CRO immediately.

Individuals relying on an interpreter are entitled to at least twice the allotted speaking time
pursuant to California Government Code, Section 11125.7, subdivision (c), and are asked to
provide at least 72 hours’ notice. Additional time for other accommodation needs may be
granted at the presiding commissioner’s discretion to ensure equitable opportunity to address
the Commission.

Meeting Expectations: Agenda and Format
Meeting Agenda
The meeting agenda outlines the planned sequence of items, during which presentations,
discussion, and public comment will occur. Each meeting includes an opportunity for public
comment on each agenda item, as well as a “general public comment” agenda item for topics
not on the agenda.

Meeting Format
During meetings, each agenda item generally follows the same format:
    •   Commission staff introduction of the item
    •   Department or other agency presentation (if applicable)
    •   Public presentation (if applicable)
    •   Commissioner questions


                                                 6

•   Tribal and other elected officials
   •   Public comment (starting first with those who have time ceded to them)
   •   Commission discussion and potential action (if applicable)

Meeting Expectations: Guidelines on Speaker Time
The Commission understands that many participants travel long distances or rearrange
commitments to attend, whether in person or remotely. To help participants prepare for
Commission meetings, we share here speaker guidelines; please keep these in mind as you
prepare your comments.

Under Commission meeting procedures, the presiding commissioner allocates a maximum
speaking time per person (one to three minutes, with exceptions) for each agenda item. The
Commission sometimes discusses items with high public engagement, potentially with large
numbers of speakers, and is committed to hearing all scheduled items, while also maximizing
the amount of information and number of viewpoints that can be shared by attendees. To
balance these goals, the presiding commissioner will seek to ensure discussions are focused,
respectful, and efficient, and that as many voices as possible can be heard.

Individual Speaking Time
At the beginning of public comment on an agenda item, the presiding commissioner will ask
staff how many speakers have indicated a desire to speak, in addition to those with time
ceded to them by other attendees (see instructions for ceded time). The presiding
commissioner will assign one to three minutes for speakers without ceded time for that
agenda item.

With limited time to speak during the meeting, it is helpful to submit detailed comments in
writing by the Comment Deadline (September 30) to help ensure that your ideas and
perspective are included in the meeting materials developed and distributed in advance.
During the meeting, you can then focus on the key points you want the commissioners to
keep in mind as they make any decisions or provide direction to staff.

Additional Time for Speakers with Ceded Time for Non-MPA Petition Items
For non-MPA petition agenda items, speakers may be approved to speak for up to five minutes
if three or more participants cede their time to them. This allows a group to designate a
spokesperson to provide comment on an agenda item. Participants ceding their time to a
spokesperson:
   •   Must be present (in person, on Zoom, or by phone) when the agenda item is called; and
   •   forego their own opportunity to speak on that agenda item.

If you plan to cede time for non-MPA petition agenda items:
   •   Pre-Register. This is the best way to ensure you are on the list of speakers, whether
       you are joining in person, via Zoom, or on the phone! No need to fill out a speaker card
       for each agenda item, no worrying about whether you have missed the queue to raise
       your hand in Zoom, and you receive confirmation via email within minutes. Pre-
       registration begins Wednesday, September 30 and ends at noon on Monday, October
       12 at https://nrm.dfg.ca.gov/FileHandler.ashx?DocumentID=247417&inline.



                                                7

•   In person. Please complete a speaker card and approach the staff table with your
       spokesperson before the agenda item begins so staff can confirm the presence of those
       ceding time. An in-person speaker may identify a remote participant who wishes to cede
       their time. However, all individuals ceding time to an in-person speaker must be present
       on Zoom or phone during the agenda item.

   •   Remote (via Zoom or phone). Remote participants who wish to cede their time must
       pre-register or notify the Commission at fgc@fgc.ca.gov by Monday, October 12 at
       noon and include the name of the individual to whom they are ceding time. All
       individuals ceding time must also be present on Zoom or phone during the agenda item.

Considerations for Giving Effective Public Comment
When addressing the Commission, begin by giving your name, any organizational affiliation,
and the number of people you represent. To help commissioners in their decision-making and
facilitate a positive meeting experience for all, please remember to:
   •   Respect the meeting environment, other speakers, staff, and commissioners.
   •   Treat all participants with courtesy and recognize diverse experiences and perspectives.
   •   Listen respectfully while one person speaks at a time.
   •   Come prepared and keep comments centered on the topic as time is limited.
   •   Focus on clear, concise contributions that support productive dialogue.
   •   If there are several speakers with the same concerns, you are encouraged to appoint a
       spokesperson to avoid repetitive comments or state your agreement with earlier
       speakers or remarks.
   •   Treat disagreements as shared problems to solve.
   •   When offering critique, propose alternative ideas when appropriate.
   •   Avoid personal accusations, stereotyping, or deliberate misinformation.

To help you organize your comments, it may be helpful to focus on:
   •   Do you support or oppose what has been proposed and why?
   •   Why is the subject important to you, your community, or your work?
   •   What action(s) would you like the Commission to consider if not what has been
       proposed?

   •   Deliberate and vote on all actions within the 15 bin 2 MPA petitions. Decisions could be
       to grant and continue to a regulatory process, deny, or take any other action the
       Commission determines is warranted by the petition such as considering regulatory
       amendments that petitioners have suggested during the petition process, or granting or
       further reviewing some portions of a petition.
   •   MPA petition agenda items will include an introduction to the subject, public comment,
       and Commission discussion and action.
   •   Ceding time will be allowed for the MPA petition agenda items (beginning with
       Agenda Item 26).

         minutes of speaking time and if four people cede their time to a spokesperson, the
         speaker will receive 2 minutes of speaking time.
       - For those attending in person, the speaker and those ceding time must submit their
         speaker cards all together at the staff table in front of the auditorium, before the
         agenda item is announced, even if you have pre-registered.
       - For those attending via Zoom, the speaker and those ceding time must either pre-
         register or send an email message to fgc@fgc.ca.gov no later than noon on Monday,
         October 12; in both cases, include your name, the spokesperson’s name, and the
         agenda item number.
   •   At any time, the presiding commissioner may ask for visual cues (such as raising hands
       or standing up) to express support or opposition.
